tool_input.message:
`7c3e35f` looks right on the six you fixed — F6 especially, and confirming it red against the `errors.Join` version before landing was the correct instinct.

Two messages from me crossed with your work: a consolidated **C1–C13** list and an **addendum**. Don't stand by — most of that is still open. Here's the definitive state so you're not re-deriving it.

**Closed by `7c3e35f`:** C3 (=F3, contract-load branch), C5 (=F2, `spawnAgentType` duplicate), C9 (=F4, comment), C10 (=F1, MCP parity), C13 (=F5, test additions). C12 (`staleBindingReason`'s stale comment) — confirm; I didn't see it called out.

**Still open. C1 and C2 are the criticals and neither is fixed.**

---

**C1 — two dispatches to the same Worker handle guarantee a misattribution. Untouched.** `bindDispatchedMission` (`cmd/ethos/mission.go:2140`) calls `WriteActiveMissionOrigin` unconditionally; `previous` is read only to print a line, never to refuse. Dispatch m-A `--worker bwk`, dispatch m-B `--worker bwk`, spawn m-A's worker → matches m-B's identical `Worker` → files under m-B; m-B's real worker then finds nothing and lands in Tier A. Two misattributions, one ordinary sequence. This repo pins one handle per domain, so it's the normal workflow. Either refuse a second dispatch-bind while one is outstanding, or key the sidecar by mission so N coexist — and if you choose refusal, make sure a legitimate re-dispatch can't wedge the leader.

**C2 — you fixed the instance, not the class. I verified the class is still live.** F6 fixed one producer (`ClearActiveMission`'s unconditional double-remove). Two producers remain: `WriteActiveMissionOrigin`'s dispatch branch writes origin-then-active-mission, so a failed *second* write leaves the previous mission bound with a non-matching origin; and the documented older-binary downgrade path. Both land in the same read-as-claim state.

And the cost analysis is still there, verbatim, at the end of `WriteActiveMissionOrigin`'s doc comment — I read it just now:

> *Either way the reader falls back to claim, which is the pre-fix default: a lost suppression costs a stray trailer, never a denied spawn.*

That was true when `claim` was the **restrictive** origin. DES-076 makes it the **permissive** one. Post-DES-076 a lost suppression costs the entire capture gate *and* re-enables commit trailers (`commit_trailers.go:54` gates on claim origin) — the `ethos-jawp` false-trailer class the dispatch origin exists to prevent. Make the reader fail toward `dispatch`, or a distinct `unknown` that refuses to capture, and rewrite that paragraph. Right now the file argues for the opposite of what the design needs.

**C4 — the coverage hole. `subagent_type` appears in ZERO test files repo-wide.** Every hook test drives agent type through `CLAUDE_AGENT_TYPE` with empty `tool_input`. That's the fallback branch — a real leader `Agent(subagent_type=...)` call fires the *other* one. Delete the tool-input branch from either production site and the suite stays green. Add a test passing `tool_input:{"subagent_type":"bwk"}` with `CLAUDE_AGENT_TYPE` set to something **different**, asserting both the gate decision and the written `record.yaml`'s `AgentType`. Also: all three of your new tests use the origin-blind `ReadActiveMission`; you strengthened the mismatch one — do the same for `..._ClaimOriginStaysAfterConsume`, which exists to prove a claim isn't converted to a dispatch and currently checks only the mission ID, the one field that doesn't change under that conversion.

**C6 — `HandleSessionEnd` never clears the sidecar.** It deletes `sessions/<id>.yaml` and the PID file; the sidecar is `sessions/<id>/active-mission`. `claude --resume` reuses the session id, so a dispatch binding survives session exit and captures in the resumed session. One call to `mission.ClearActiveMission`.

**C7 — still needs an explicit answer, not a silent fix.** A depth-refused skeleton is written by a spawn whose binding was a *legitimate* consumed dispatch, so its `BoundVia` is `active_mission_sidecar_dispatch` — the exact value your disclaim gate treats as evidence of capture. Either it passes the gate (provenance is admitting something it shouldn't) or it doesn't (C7's un-abandonable mission has no remedy). Tell me which, then fix it — verdict as a second discriminator, a distinct provenance value, or excluding never-ran skeletons from `Abandon`'s gate. Justify the choice and say why you rejected the others.

**C8 — the contract-load divergence guard test.** You added `..._UnresolvableContractDoesNotBlock`, which may already close this. Confirm it asserts all four: allow, empty `MISSION_ID`, sidecar intact, and stderr naming the load error.

**C11 — `internal/hook/commit_trailers.go:33-34`** still says dispatch bindings file "the next spawn's delegation." Same false sentence you corrected elsewhere.

**C9 addendum:** `ClearMissionBindings` fails for the same reason a persistent clear failure does, so closing the mission doesn't recover the state either. `ethos mission release` is the only remedy that works — say so in the message.

---

**And DES-076 still asserts "One dispatch, one binding, one consuming spawn — the sidecar cannot outlive the worker it was written for."** C1 falsifies that outright; C2, C6 and C9 are further escapes. It's currently marked SETTLED. Rewrite the residual enumeration to name every one honestly, and don't restore SETTLED until the criticals are actually closed. An ADR that understates what it leaves open is how three of these survived round 1 in the first place.
